value.rationale: The paper explicitly motivates deletion/addition beyond coordinate examples. This finding gives a natural complete dual-projective geometric classification of when a fixed k-conic nearly-free pencil remains free/nearly-free after adding arbitrary lines, with a sharp three-level Jacobian-defect jump, and isolates a genuinely nonquasihomogeneous local phenomenon indispensable to the classification. It is neither a coordinate-case repetition nor a one-off numerical census; it holds for every k>=2.
